paragraphs: Storm Boelo hit Ireland on Saturday. It brought heavy rain and very strong winds.
There is an orange wind warning for Donegal until 9am on Sunday. There are yellow wind warnings for Connacht, Cavan, Louth and Monaghan until 10am. Donegal has a yellow warning until 3pm.
Trees may fall. Some homes may lose power. Roads, buses and ferries may have problems.
The ground is very wet after Storm Austen. So rivers and the sea can still flood. Nine coastal counties have flood warnings. The sea will be dangerous until Sunday night.
Stay away from the coast. Put away bins and garden chairs. Do not walk in the hills. Charge your phone. Only travel if you must. In an emergency, call 112 or 999.
Storm Boelo brought heavy rain and strong winds to Ireland on Saturday, only days after Storm Austen. Some warnings continue into Sunday, so people in the north-west should be careful.

Met Éireann's orange wind warning for Donegal lasts until 9am on Sunday. Yellow wind warnings cover Connacht, Cavan, Louth and Monaghan until 10am, and Donegal until 3pm. On Saturday, Kerry and Galway also had orange rain warnings, and the wind warning reached Dublin, where the marathon takes place on Sunday.
The winds can bring down trees and power lines, and make driving very difficult. Some ferry sailings were cancelled on Saturday. Gale warnings stay in place for all coasts until 10pm on Sunday.

Flooding is still a risk. The ground is full of water after Storm Austen, and high tides can push the sea onto land. Nine coastal counties have flood warnings, and big rivers may keep rising after the rain stops.
Officials advise people to stay away from the coast, tie down loose objects, avoid hill walking, charge phones and travel only if necessary. In an emergency, call 112 or 999.

Storm Boelo swept across Ireland on Saturday with torrential rain and damaging gusts, arriving just days after Storm Austen. Several warnings remain in force on Sunday, particularly in the north-west.

Met Éireann's Status Orange wind warning for Donegal runs until 9am on Sunday, with yellow wind warnings for Connacht, Cavan, Louth and Monaghan until 10am and for Donegal until 3pm. On Saturday, Kerry and Galway were also under orange rain warnings, and a yellow wind warning was extended to Dublin ahead of Sunday's marathon.

Forecasters warned of fallen trees, damage to power lines, outages and very difficult driving conditions. Several ferry sailings were cancelled on Saturday, and gale warnings remain in place for all coasts until 10pm on Sunday.

The flood risk has not passed. Saturated ground and high tides mean coastal and river flooding is possible, and nine coastal counties are under flood warnings. Larger rivers may continue to rise after the rain eases.
Emergency planners urge the public to avoid coastal areas, secure loose items, postpone hill walking, charge mobile phones and travel only if essential. In an emergency, call 112 or 999.

Forecasters cautioned that uprooted trees, stricken power lines and treacherous roads were all likely. Ferry crossings were scrapped on Saturday, and gale warnings will remain in place on every coast until 10pm on Sunday.

The danger of flooding has yet to abate. Waterlogged ground coupled with high tides leaves coastal and riverside areas vulnerable, prompting flood warnings in nine coastal counties, and larger rivers may continue to swell well after the rain relents.
